messages:
maya: Quick idea — we should formalize a lightweight crosswalk that ties metrics to traces for cost attribution without exploding cardinality. thinking: a sparse propagated cost token + local rollups at ingest. :thinking:

jon: Can you sketch the token? how sparse are we talking?

maya: token = 8-12 hex chars, not attached to every event. only propagated on request entry when tenant has billable activity. keep it optional so SDKs dont bloat. example header: `X-Cost-Token: b4f7a2c9`

nisha: optional propagation is good. main risk: sampling will drop the token and our rollups mismatch. how do we reconcile sampled traces vs metric counters?

maya: plan — two parallel paths: (1) metrics path still emits per-tenant counters (low-card compacted) and (2) traces carry token used to attribute high-fidelity spans back to a tenant cohort. then reconcile with probabilistic uplift factors computed daily.

lee: probabilistic uplift sounds reasonable. what's the ingest cost? adding token to spans increases indexable fields — can we keep token out of primary index? store it in payload blob and build a sparse index only for tokens seen > N times.

jon: +1 for sparse indexing. we can maintain a hot set for frequent tokens and GC the rest. also consider using a bloom filter for quick membership tests during query time instead of full index lookup.

maya: exactly. bloom filter for fast routing, then fall back to blob scan for small results. this keeps write path cheap.

nisha: query semantics: product wants daily cost per-tenant and ad-hoc drilldown for spikes. uplift math needs provenance. we should store: token -> tenant mapping change log, sampling rate, and uplift factor per day.

maya: agree. record a minimal reconciliation artifact: `date, token, tenant_id, sample_rate, uplift_factor` — append-only, small table.

lee: we should also think about multi-model requests that fan out to many backend models. token should be sticky per top-level request not per sub-call. otherwise cost attribution fragments.

jon: good point. SDKs should set token once at request ingress and pass it through internal async calls, but not reassign. add a server-side guard: if multiple tokens appear in same top-level trace, mark trace as "multi-token" and route for manual review.

ingest-bot: deploy check: tracer v2 (edge) has 120ms p95 overhead target. adding token storage and bloom-check adds ~0.6ms on average in local testing.

nisha: 0.6ms on edge is fine. bigger concern is cardinality of the reconciliation table. estimates? if tokens are per-tenant-per-day and we have 5k tenants => 5k rows/day, fine. if tokens per-session => explode.

maya: enforce policy: token issuance limited to tenant-configured sampling cohort or billing-enabled routes. default: token per-tenant-per-day, with opt-in for higher fidelity.

lee: implementation spike for ingest:
```
- accept X-Cost-Token header (optional)
- attach token to trace payload but not primary index
- check bloom filter for hot tokens -> route to hot index
- write reconciliation row once per token/day
```

jon: next steps: id owners for SDKs (maya), ingest plumbing (lee), uplift computation + storage (nisha). small RFC + 2-week spike.

maya: tagging action items: @lee will prototype bloom-filter path, @nisha will draft reconciliation schema, i'll update SDK docs and prod-playbook. sync Thursday. :+1:

nisha: one more: telemetry privacy — token must be opaque and not carry tenant PII. use HSM-signed mapping only available to billing-service.

maya: yep — token is opaque. mapping stored in billing service only. logs should redact the mapping.

jon: sounds good. thumbs up on RFC + spike.

maya: thanks all — filing short RFC after this thread. link: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/metrics-trace-crosswalk (WIP)
